Wire protocols squeeze small integers into few bytes by folding the sign bit into the value and splitting the result into seven-bit groups. Small negative numbers become small unsigned ones, so they stay cheap. Decoding must be just as careful as encoding: truncated or padded byte groups are malformed, not creative.
